_note: Open analytical questions (no single right answer). Each lists the KEY CONSIDERATIONS a thorough answer should surface. Metric = coverage: how many of these each approach raises. This tests Orlog's real value (surface every angle), objectively, instead of 'pick the correct action'.

questions.text: I'm about to launch my product next week. What could go wrong?
Should our small team build our own database or use an existing one?
considerations: how well an existing option already fits

questions.text: I'm thinking of moving to a new city for a job. What should I weigh?
considerations: how stable the job actually is
distance from family and support network
what happens if it doesn't work out
impact on a partner or family

questions.text: We're deciding whether to fire an underperforming but long-tenured employee. What matters?
considerations: whether the performance is actually fixable
cost and disruption of replacing them
the precedent it sets for others
whether the role itself is still needed

questions.text: Should I take on debt to expand my business?
considerations: return on investment vs the interest cost
whether cash flow can service the debt
how certain the added demand really is
the downside if the expansion fails

questions.text: A new technology could disrupt our industry. How should we respond?
considerations: adopt now versus wait and see
what competitors are likely to do
the chance the technology never matures
